correctness.rationale: All quantifiers fixed and reconstructible. The finite permutation-group commutant reduces to the \(2^r\) algebra generated by coordinate averages, giving the unique equivariant projection and global minimality. The kernel coefficient and multiplicity count yield exact ℓ∞ and ℓ1 norms. The CLT plus LLN yields Hermite coefficients while L² orthogonality proves uniform integrability. Check extracted standalone Python package for exact small cases; no empirical step is needed for the infinite claims.

value.rationale: An exact best-projection stability invariant for multivariate low-order interactions on arbitrary finite Cartesian alphabets. Intermediate degrees are a motivated finite-product decomposition gap identified explicitly in 2025 literature; endpoint constants and sharp \(r^{d/2}\) Gaussian growth are quantitative, nontrivial, and independently useful for the size of low-order component extraction. Not a mere renaming of Krawtchouk convergence or Rudin averaging.
